Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record

This bill is part of a package that would create a new vehicle efficiency standard (NVES) for Australia to reduce carbon dioxide emissions from new cars, SUVs, utes and vans, and encourage the supply of low and zero emissions vehicles.
The NVES would set annual CO2 emissions targets for vehicle suppliers, rewarding those below the target with credits and penalising those above after a two-year period to reduce their emissions.
The bill specifies emissions targets for calendar years 2025 to 2029, with targets for later years to be set by the minister, and a review of the scheme is planned for 2026.
Establishes a new vehicle efficiency standard (NVES) for Australia.
Sets CO2 emissions targets for each regulated year, with credits for suppliers below the target and civil penalties for those above after a two-year period.
Enables the minister to set emissions targets for vehicle suppliers for years after 2029 via a legislative instrument.
Triggers the Regulatory Powers (Standard Provisions) Act 2014 for compliance and enforcement.
Allows the secretary to compel production of information or documents and seek adverse publicity orders or non-punitive orders from a court.
Includes mechanisms to adjust targets for vehicle weight and to apply a higher CO2 target for light commercial vehicles.
Vehicle suppliers bringing new cars, SUVs, utes and vans to the Australian market.
